name: BRAGG, Andrew James

headline.note: Private accounting work and a later private-company managing-director spell are documented, but substantive full-time status and complete dates are not. Financial Services Council and Business Council roles are employer-association work; Menzies, Liberal Party and campaign roles are separately excluded. Missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official biography records a BAcc from ANU; enrolment/completion dates, study load and concurrent work are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official frozen biography records employment in 2008; biographies identify accounting/internal audit. Exact dates, employing EY entity, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private control is clear, but year-only dates and unknown full-time status do not support a headline duration.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official frozen biography supplies title and year endpoints. FSC describes itself as a peak body for financial-services member companies. Exact dates, title transitions, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Employer-association work is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Director of Policy (also reported as Policy and Global Markets)
career_spells.evidence_note: Official frozen biography supplies title and year endpoints; other biographies place departure in 2016, creating a year-label ambiguity retained for follow-up. Exact dates, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Employer-association work is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Qualification is documented and reportedly undertaken during FSC employment; dates and study load are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded; no employment FTE inferred.

career_spells.role: Director of Policy and Research / Policy Director
career_spells.evidence_note: Official biography records the role in 2016–2017; secondary sources place commencement in November 2016 and the subsequent BCA role in August 2017. Exact days, hours and leave remain unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Liberal-aligned party-policy organisation work is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Contemporaneous reporting and the official biography establish acting appointment from April 2017. Exact cessation date, employment/secondment relationship to Menzies, hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party-organisation employment is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official party biography and first speech establish national-director responsibility during the 2017 postal survey. Payroll, exact dates, hours and overlap with BCA/Menzies are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party/campaign work is excluded and not added to overlapping spells.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official frozen biography gives 2017–2018; public professional-profile index refines the role to August 2017–August 2018. Hours and leave are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Employer-association work is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional-profile index gives month endpoints and managing-director title; ABR confirms the Australian private company. Activities, remuneration, substantive hours and campaign overlap are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Private/self-employed classification is supported, but substantive full-time work is not; no headline duration counted.

career_spells.employer: Liberal Party of Australia / Senate campaign (payroll entity unresolved)
career_spells.role: Endorsed Liberal candidate for the Senate
career_spells.evidence_note: Public professional-profile index identifies the candidate period, overlapping Bragg PPC. Candidacy itself does not establish paid employment, payroll entity or hours.
career_spells.counting_note: Party/campaign activity is excluded; no employment status inferred.

career_spells.role: Senator for New South Wales; parliamentary and shadow roles nested within service
career_spells.evidence_note: Official sources record Senate service from 1 July 2019, ongoing at the frozen snapshot. Committee and shadow portfolios are nested duties, not additive employment spells.
career_spells.counting_note: Elected office is excluded under the codebook.

open_questions: What are the exact dates, employing EY entity, substantive hours and leave for the 2008 accounting spell?
Why does the frozen FSC endpoint say 2017 while other accounts place departure in 2016, and what were the exact promotion dates/hours?
Were the Menzies, acting Liberal federal-director and Yes-campaign roles separate employment, secondments or overlapping duties, and which entity paid him?
What services, remuneration and substantive hours applied to Bragg PPC during the overlapping Senate campaign?
What were the ANU and Macquarie study dates and any concurrent paid work?
